title: Enquirer’s Guide: Has anyone sent something inside?
author: The Enquirer’s Guide Desk
paragraphs: This entry from The Enquirer’s Guide answers a question often put to the Society: “Has anyone sent something inside?”

In 1844 a stable aperture admitted a tethered brass probe, which returned carrying a pale mineral deposit. Later probes and expeditions extended the surveys, although every crossing still demands careful records of what went out and what came back.

Readers should treat the answer as an introduction rather than a final authority. Eidetic science in Alderwick is reported through measurements, disputed interpretations and careful revisions, and a respectable enquiry may properly end with further questions.
